extracted.intended_audience: communication scholars, development planners, educational technologists, and policymakers working on mass-media and national development
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for designing, implementing, and assessing communication and educational-media programs aimed at accelerating economic, social, and political development in emerging nations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systems approach to communication and development
rubrics_metrics.description: Conceptualize society as a boundary-maintaining set of interdependent components; both independent and dependent variables in research can be structural features rather than individual traits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a systems analysis perspective: 'By interdependence we mean a relationship of parts ... anything happening to one component of a system affects ... the balance and relationship of the whole system. By boundary-maintaining we mean a state in which the components are so related that it is possible to tell where the system ends and its environment begins.' Design studies and interventions with attention to structural interrelations among communication, economic, political and social structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feeling of nationhood
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be a feeling of nationhood for communication to contribute to economic growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schramm lists this as a cognitive functional requisite: without national identity a nation 'cannot pierce the economic barrier.' Programs should assess and, where appropriate, cultivate a sense of nationhood among target populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to defer gratification
rubrics_metrics.description: A population must be willing to defer gratifications until the nation as a whole can afford them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider communication strategies that foster acceptance of delayed or collective benefits rather than immediate individual consumption as part of development-oriented messaging and education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of group/national goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance of group or national goals over some individual goals is necessary for development-oriented communication to be effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should promote shared goals and collective aims where appropriate; evaluate audience receptivity to collective vs. individual goal framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding purpose of effort
rubrics_metrics.description: People must understand why they are making an effort as a prerequisite for communication to facilitate economic development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design messages that clearly explain the rationale and expected outcomes of development actions to increase buy-in and sustained participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feeling of participation in decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be a feeling that people have a part in determining what should be done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include participatory elements in communication and planning so audiences perceive agency and involvement; measure perceived participation as part of program evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition of new skills and knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquiring new skills and knowledge is necessary for economic development and should be an objective of communication programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize educational content and capacity-building; use mass media to teach skills where teachers or other delivery systems are inadequate (e.g., 'substitute for the teacher not yet trained and to support the teacher not yet trained well enough'). Evaluate learning outcomes and skill acquisition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of effective market (structural requisite)
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be an extension of the effective market to accommodate economic development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether communication and infrastructural changes are enlarging market reach and enabling exchanges needed for development; incorporate market-extension measures into planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and acceptance of new roles and role relations
rubrics_metrics.description: New roles must be designated and accepted, bringing new responsibilities and role relations as part of structural requisites for development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should anticipate social-role changes and include measures to facilitate role specification, training, and social acceptance of new roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material and institutional prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication development depends on material support (equipment, supplies), managerial support (qualified personnel), and financial support (advertising income, literate readership).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before implementing media programs, evaluate and secure the necessary equipment, logistics, personnel training, and sustainable financing. Recognize that without these supports communication development cannot be sustained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural fit and no universal sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not assume a universal sequence of development; choose strategies that fit the nation's social structure and cultural background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select media and approaches depending on task, audience, and resources; avoid one-size-fits-all sequencing and design culturally appropriate interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate media selection (Big Media vs Little Media)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Big Media are not necessarily preferable to the Little Media; media choice should depend on task, audience, resources, and group processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate which media best reach and influence target audiences given context and constraints; explicitly consider group processes in media design and deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions of mass media in development
rubrics_metrics.description: Mass media can be used to widen horizons, raise aspirations, focus attention, create a climate for development, feed interpersonal channels, and act as teachers to break the bonds of ignorance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing programs, identify which of these functions is primary (e.g., aspiration-raising vs. direct instruction) and tailor content, format, and evaluation metrics accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use mass media to support/ substitute for teachers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use mass media to substitute for or support teachers who are not yet trained or are underqualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design instructional television, radio, or programmed materials specifically to deliver or reinforce curriculum where teacher capacity is limited; evaluate classroom and learning impacts in pilot studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective decision criteria and cost-effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide educational planners with objective criteria and rigorous appraisals (including cost-effectiveness) to guide decisions about introducing educational media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use world-wide surveys, case studies, multiple measures, and cost-effectiveness analyses (as Schramm's UNESCO work and subsequent projects did) to inform policy and funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple measures in evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Program evaluations should provide multiple measures on impact (e.g., learning outcomes, behavioral change, system-level effects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt mixed-measure evaluation designs (quantitative and qualitative) as done in the Colombia Peace Corps evaluation to capture diverse impacts and inform R&D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political sensitivity and risk assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication development does not automatically lead to greater freedom; it can be used equally well for indoctrination or democratization depending on political context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess political implications, risks of centralized control, and likely effects on press freedom and civic participation; design safeguards or complementary governance reforms where increased communication capacity might be monopolized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pragmatism and urgency in research and action
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should be practical and oriented to solving pressing human needs; act on adequate evidence rather than waiting for perfect knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ rigorous methods (scientific sampling, design, statistics) but prioritize timely, actionable experiments and sharing of results—'we must try to leap ahead to more crucial experiments now'—balancing scientific rigor with practical urgency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-fertilization and collaboration with educators/planners
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek collaboration between communication researchers and educators/planners to ensure programs are educationally and administratively relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build partnerships (e.g., Schramm's association with Stanford's School of Education) so doctoral students and programs produce planners and decision-makers, not only technologists; incorporate educational expertise in program design and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate technological leapfrogging
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing countries can skip intermediate technologies when appropriate (e.g., move directly to photosetting or satellite-based solutions) if new methods promise savings in time and money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether newer devices/methods are appropriate and cost-effective for local conditions and whether they will 'save time and money, and get the information flowing more efficiently' before adopting leapfrog technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious about universal prescriptions; emphasize local adaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no single strategy universally applicable; choices should be made considering local social structure and cultural background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid blanket prescriptions; pilot interventions, adapt to local circumstances, and allow multiple possible development pathways depending on context.
